st.headline: SK Hynix, Samsung shares rally after report Temasek to invest
st.teaser: Asia Business Daily reported that Temasek plans to invest directly in the two chipmakers.
fullText: SEOUL - South Korean chipmakers rallied as risk appetite returns after July’s rout , with a local media report of investment plans by Singapore’s Temasek supporting sentiment.

Shares of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix extended gains to more than 8 per cent, after Asia Business Daily reported that Temasek plans to invest directly in the two chipmakers through its internal investment team, and is mulling timing. The benchmark Kospi gained as much as 5.1 per cent.

The chipmakers saw a brutal sell-off in July as doubts grew over the pace of rapid AI infrastructure buildout, leading to an unwinding of leveraged positions. The shares have been rebounding recently, amid growing expectations the companies will bolster shareholder returns with buybacks and more dividends.

SK Hynix on Aug 7 said it will unveil shareholder-return details in the third quarter. Samsung Electronics is expected to follow suit, with KB Securities analysts expecting a more than tenfold increase in shareholder returns.
Temasek didn’t immediately comment on the report when contacted by Bloomberg.

“This hints at long-term investors’ improving appetite for South Korea’s deeply-undervalued semiconductor sector,” said Homin Lee, a senior macro strategist at Lombard Odier Singapore. “More aggressive foreign institutions are likely to view these key names as an opportunity, especially if retail-driven volatility subsides.”

The valuations of the memory chipmakers have come down to record low levels following the July rout. Samsung and SK Hynix are trading at 4.2 and 3.6 times forward earnings, respectively, compared with more than 21 times for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index of global chip peers.
Global funds added more than 2 trillion won ($1.4 billion) worth of Kospi shares as of mid-Wednesday, while retail traders sold.

If confirmed, the investment would signal “strong foreign confidence in Korea’s AI/memory cycle,” said Ha SeokKeun, chief investment officer at Eugene Asset Management. It would be one of the drivers supporting a Kospi rebound, he added. BLOOMBERG

cna.headline: Bell backs injured Suaalii to return to Wallabies colours in no time
cna.teaser: Bell backs injured Suaalii to return to Wallabies colours in no time
fullText: SYDNEY, Aug 12 : Wallabies prop Angus Bell has backed Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to be playing again sooner rather than later after the centre suffered another injury setback against Japan last weekend.
Suaalii will miss this weekend's return match against Japan in Townsville after picking up a minor hamstring strain in last Saturday's 35-32 win in Osaka.
The 23-year-old has been bedevilled by injuries since making a big-money switch from rugby league in late 2024, and Bell said it was certainly nothing to do with the way he looked after himself.
"There's one thing that I've never questioned Su on, it's his preparation," Bell told reporters from Queensland on Wednesday.

"It's honestly just probably a bit of maturing in the body. I went through the exact same thing, I went through two and a half to three years where I wasn't playing any rugby for the Waratahs, which was tough.
"But it's only a really minor injury, he'll be back sooner rather than later so we look forward to having him back."
Josh Flook was called into the squad as cover and inside centre Hunter Paisami said the team had a "next up" approach to losing players as they looked towards the second test.
"Whoever's in that 12 and 13 jersey, we just know that they will do a job for the boys and for the jersey," he said.
Paisami's Queensland Reds teammate Carter Gordon is also tipped to return at flyhalf on Saturday after recovering from a calf injury.
Declan Meredith endured a tricky night in the number 10 shirt in Osaka so Gordon looks likely to be up against Ben Donaldson in the race for the starting playmaker role.
"I think he's just a natural 10," Paisami said of Gordon.

"They all are natural 10s, but I feel like they're just very similar. Obviously, Carter's defensive side. He's a big body and he puts his body on the line. They all read the game pretty well. If Carter is in it's a huge plus."
New coach Les Kiss will name his team on Thursday.
A single handpicked story that we think you shouldn't miss. Just one a day.

listening.title: The Evolution of Singapore's Heritage Hawker Stalls
listening.transcript: Many young Singaporeans are stepping up to preserve the nation's cherished hawker culture. Facing long working hours and rising ingredient costs, these next-generation hawkers are leveraging modern marketing and tech to stay competitive. While traditionalists worry about losing original flavors, these pioneers argue that adaptation is key to survival in a modern global hub. The government has also rolled out subsidies to ease their transition.

economistArticle.title: Hooray for index funds—just don’t call them passive
paras: For decades, index funds have been heralded as the ultimate financial equalizer. Created by Vanguard founder Jack Bogle in the 1970s, these instruments promised to democratize wealth creation. By tracking broad market indices like the S&P 500, they allowed ordinary retail investors to capture the collective return of corporate America without paying exorbitant fees to active fund managers. Today, trillions of dollars reside in passive vehicles, reshaping global capital markets.

However, to describe indexing as "passive" is a misnomer that obscures a complicated reality. The composition of any index is fundamentally an active construct. Stock market indices do not appear spontaneously from the ether; they are designed, maintained, and occasionally modified by committee decisions. For instance, the inclusion or exclusion of a company like Tesla in a major index involves highly qualitative judgments about corporate governance, liquidity, and profitability.

Furthermore, index fund providers themselves exercise tremendous discretionary power. Far from being inert pipelines, giants like BlackRock, Vanguard, and State Street wield immense voting power in corporate boardrooms. As major shareholders in almost every public firm, these institutional behemoths actively engage with management on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) policies. The decisions they make regarding board appointments and climate resolutions are anything but passive.

The rise of index-centric investing has also altered price-discovery mechanisms on Wall Street. Critics argue that when capital flows blindly into stocks based solely on their market capitalization, it creates systemic distortions. This can lead to a self-reinforcing cycle where already-dominant tech giants receive an outsized share of investment, starvation-rationing capital for smaller, innovative enterprises. Hence, passive indexing might inadvertently undermine market efficiency.

Ultimately, the moniker "passive" belies the constant calibration required to navigate modern financial waters. Investors who opt for passive funds are still making a deliberate asset-allocation choice. They choose which indexes to track, when to rebalance, and how to allocate between equities and bonds. In a world of infinite financial complexity, Bogle’s revolution was not about eliminating human choice, but about transferring the power of those choices from Wall Street middlemen to individual savers.
economistArticle.cn:
几十年来，指数基金一直被誉为终极的财务平等工具。这些工具由先锋集团（Vanguard）创始人杰克·博格尔（Jack Bogle）在20世纪70年代创立，承诺让财富创造走向民主化。通过追踪标普500等广泛的市场指数，它们让普通散户投资者能够获取美国企业界整体的集体回报，而无需向主动型基金经理支付高昂的费用。如今，数万亿美元沉淀在这些被动工具中，重塑了全球资本市场。
然而，将被动指数化描述为“被动”其实是一个误称，遮蔽了复杂的现实。任何指数的构成从根本上说都是一种主动的建构。股市指数并非凭空出现；它们是通过委员会的决策进行设计、维护并偶尔修改的。例如，将特斯拉这样的公司纳入或排除在某项主要指数之外，涉及对公司治理、流动性和盈利能力的极具定性的判断。
此外，指数基金提供商本身也行使着巨大的自由裁量权。黑石（BlackRock）、先锋和道富（State Street）等巨头绝非毫无生机的传导管道，它们在企业董事会中拥有巨大的投票权。作为几乎所有上市公司的主要股东，这些机构巨头积极在环境、社会和治理（ESG）政策上与管理层进行交涉。它们在董事会任命和气候决议方面所做的决定，绝非被动。
以指数为中心的投资兴起，也改变了华尔街的价格发现机制。批评者认为，当资本仅根据市值盲目流入股票时，会造成系统性扭曲。这可能导致自我强化的循环，使已经占据主导地位的科技巨头获得不成比例的投资份额，从而使规模较小、具有创新精神的企业陷入资金极度匮乏的窘境。因此，被动指数投资可能会在无意中损害市场效率。
归根结底，“被动”这一绰号掩盖了驾驭现代金融浪潮所需的持续调整。选择被动基金的投资者仍然在做出刻意的资产配置选择。他们选择追踪哪些指数、何时重新平衡，以及如何在股票和债券之间进行分配。在无限金融复杂性的世界里，博格尔的革命并不是为了消除人类的选择，而是为了将这些选择的权利从华尔街的中间商手中转移到个人储户手中。

gems.s: Stock market indices do not appear spontaneously from the ether; they are designed, maintained, and occasionally modified by committee decisions.
gems.why: This sentence uses a strong semicolon connection and a vivid spatial metaphor ("from the ether") to debunk a common misconception. 该句运用分号连接与生动的空间比喻（“凭空出现”），有力地打破了普遍的误解。

gems.s: In a world of infinite financial complexity, Bogle’s revolution was not about eliminating human choice, but about transferring the power of those choices from Wall Street middlemen to individual savers.
gems.why: The sentence employs a highly effective "not about..., but about..." parallel structure to contrast the traditional view of passive investing with its true democratic impact. 该句采用经典的“不是……而是……”排比结构，将对被动投资的传统看法与其真正的民主化影响进行对比，极具说服力。
